method:
Finite-volume copper sheets, distributed ordinary via barrels and perforated TIM.

No solder-fill, FR4, plastic-top or air-conduction credit. Source is isothermal
over the mask opening (an approximation, not proof of partial solder wetting).
Via conduction is distributed around the hole circumference instead of a
mesh-dependent point contact. Hole areas reduce sheet/TIM conductance. Actual
die heat flux, localized voids and Cu/via transitions remain unvalidated.
limitations: Joint resistance and wetting NOT measured;1K/W is an acceptance assumption, not a guaranteed joint
Isothermal source and homogeneous Cu cannot bound localized void hot spots
No solder fill credited; barrel10um is a sensitivity, not a guaranteed JLC minimum
Circumferential via coupling, perforated sheet approximation and mesh extrapolation are not validated FEM
Sink natural convection depends on orientation and enclosure. No closed enclosure performance claimed
